title: Tenant-ratecap adaptive phase controller for latency-fair throughput
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Develop an adaptive per-tenant phase controller that dynamically adjusts prefill/decode phase split and tenant rate caps to meet tenant SLOs while maximizing cluster throughput and kernel utilization. The controller should combine latency SLO feedback, token budget windows, and signals from kernel selection and attention-sparsity probes to decide: (1) whether to split a request into finer-grained phases, (2) whether to throttle or prioritize a tenant in the current timeslice, and (3) when to prefer lower-cost kernel paths or quantized model variants for opportunistic throughput. This ticket covers design, simulation, and a safe canary rollout plan.
background: Current static phase-splitting heuristics cause two recurring problems: (A) tenants with aggressive throughput needs can monopolize microphase slots causing high tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants; (B) kernel-selection churn increases due to uncoordinated phase merges/splits, hurting GPU occupancy. Existing solutions (quota-based hedging, fixed phase thresholds) reduce one problem at the expense of the other. We need a feedback-driven controller that balances latency fairness and throughput across tenants and reduces unnecessary kernel switching by making phase decisions aware of kernel costs and attention sparsity hints.
proposal: Create a controller service that runs per-runtime-node and/or as a centralized policy agent. Key components: (a) tenant SLO store and short-term token budgets; (b) phase-split estimator using sequence-length, prefill density, and attention-sparsity probe; (c) kernel-cost estimator (estimated ms/token for candidate kernels) fed by recent kernel telemetry; (d) decision module that emits: split_threshold, tenant_priority_score, and kernel_preference_hint. The controller should expose a lightweight RPC to the scheduler to influence microbatch formation and to the kernel selector to bias kernel choice. Controller decisions must be deterministic for reproducibility and log-sampled for auditing.
metrics: fairness index: ratio of latency SLO violations across top 10 tenants
accuracy/regression delta on standard eval prompts (to detect quality loss when preferring cheaper kernels)
acceptance_criteria: Controller prototype runs in simulation and produces deterministic decisions given identical input traces
Simulation shows >=20% reduction in p99 latency for latency-sensitive tenants under mixed workload compared to baseline, without reducing cluster throughput by more than 8%
Kernel-switch rate decreases by at least 15% in mixed-attention workloads in simulation
End-to-end integration test with scheduler and kernel selector passes without deadlocks or priority inversion
Canary rollout plan exists with automated rollback conditions based on SLO and kernel error rates

simulation_plan: Use the anonymized 7-day production trace used by perf-team. Replay at target cluster scale in the simulator with current static phase-split policy as baseline. Evaluate scenarios: (1) mixed latency-sensitive and throughput tenants; (2) attention-sparsity skewed workloads; (3) spike/dropping load patterns. Run sensitivity sweeps over controller hyperparameters (split aggressiveness, tenant penalty weight, kernel-pref bias) and record metric curves. Produce CSV exports and Jupyter notebooks for analysis.
experiments: Microbench: probe attention-sparsity vs kernel exec time across GPUs and quantizations
A/B sim: controller vs baseline on archived traces
Kernel-cost ablation: controller enabled but without kernel hints
Tenant-prioritization ablation: static weights vs adaptive budgets
rollout_plan: 1) Integration tests in CI. 2) Dark-launch controller decisions (log-only) for two weeks in one cell. 3) Canary: enable controller adjudication on 5% of requests in one cell with strict rollback rules. 4) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% for the cell if metrics pass. 5) Gradual cross-cell rollout with monitoring of cross-tenant fairness metrics. Rollback triggers: >2x baseline p99 for any latency-SLO tenant, >5% GPU error increase, or >20% drop in throughput for 10 minutes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Controller could introduce oscillations in tenant priority leading to instability. Mitigation: implement hysteresis and rate limit policy updates; require minimum hold time for decisions.
Risk: Incorrect kernel hints might degrade model output quality. Mitigation: restrict kernel-preference to safe variants in first canary; run quality evals on a fixed prompt set before widening.
Risk: Added RPC surface increases latency. Mitigation: embed inexpensive cached decisions in scheduler loop and only refresh asynchronously.
Risk: Determinism loss across nodes. Mitigation: include a stable seed and versioned policy payloads, and log decisions for replayability.
